title: Invertibility of the canonical commutative-ring slice inverse mate
statement: Let $(D,K)$ and $(C,J)$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and $u:D\to C$ continuous with finite-limit-preserving inverse image on set sheaves. Fix $V\in D$ and assume the induced $u_V:D/V\to C/u(V)$ is continuous for the localized topologies [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let $L,L_V$ be the chosen left adjoints on sheaves of commutative rings to precomposition $P,P_V$. Let $j_V,j_U$ be sectionwise restriction, where $U=u(V)$. The direct-image comparison $b:Pj_V\cong j_UP_V$ is identity on every section. The inverse mate $j_VL_V\to Lj_U$ of $b$, formed using the chosen sheaf adjunctions, is an isomorphism. Here the inverse mate at A is adjunct to $j_V(\eta_A)$ followed by $b_{L A}$. This is a statement about that specified map, not just existence of some comparison.

proof.text: Use the proved normalized set inverse mate and the proved finite-limit preservation theorem for localized set inverse image from the set comparison module.

Construct the lifted ring adjunction from the product-preserving set inverse image using the sectionwise equivalence with internal ring objects. Transport by uniqueness of left adjoints, retaining the unit normalization for the forgetful comparison.

Use the unit equations and injectivity of the localized set adjunction to identify the underlying ring comparison, conjugated by the normalized forgetful isomorphisms, with sliceSetPullbackMap. The forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms, so every component and hence the ring natural transformation is invertible.
